title: Grade 9 Mathematics — Lines and Angles & Triangles
description: Lines and Angles and Triangles practice questions
subject: mathematics

questions.question: If two lines intersect, the vertically opposite angles are:
questions.explanation: When two lines intersect, the vertically opposite angles (across the vertex) are always equal. This is a fundamental theorem in geometry.

questions.question: The sum of angles on a straight line is:
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line are called linear pairs. They always add up to 180° (supplementary angles).

questions.question: If a transversal cuts two parallel lines, alternate interior angles are:
questions.explanation: When a transversal cuts parallel lines, alternate interior angles (Z-angles) are equal. This is the alternate interior angles theorem.

questions.question: Co-interior angles (same-side interior angles) formed by a transversal cutting two parallel lines are:
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles (also called consecutive interior angles) formed by a transversal cutting two parallel lines are supplementary — they add up to 180°.

questions.question: In the figure, two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. If one co-interior angle is 65°, the other is:
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles sum to 180°. So the other angle = 180° − 65° = 115°.

questions.question: The complement of an angle of 37° is:
questions.explanation: Complementary angles sum to 90°. So complement = 90° − 37° = 53°.

If one angle of a linear pair is twice the other, the angles are:
questions.explanation: Let angles be x and 2x. x + 2x = 180° → 3x = 180° → x = 60°. Angles are 60° and 120°.

questions.question: The sum of angles of a triangle is:
questions.explanation: The angle sum property of triangles: the sum of all three interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.

questions.question: Two triangles are congruent if two sides and the included angle of one triangle are equal to those of another. This is the:
questions.explanation: SAS (Side-Angle-Side) congruence: if two sides and the angle between them (included angle) of one triangle equal the corresponding parts of another, the triangles are congruent.

questions.question: An exterior angle of a triangle equals:
options: The sum of all three interior angles
The sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles
The supplement of the adjacent interior angle
Half the sum of the interior angles
questions.explanation: The Exterior Angle Theorem: an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote (non-adjacent) interior angles.

questions.question: In △PQR, PQ = PR. Then:
questions.explanation: In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite to equal sides are equal. Since PQ = PR, the angles opposite to them (∠R and ∠Q respectively) are equal: ∠Q = ∠R.

questions.question: In a right triangle, the side opposite the right angle is called the:
questions.explanation: The side opposite the 90° angle in a right triangle is the hypotenuse — it is always the longest side of the right triangle.

questions.question: If the exterior angle of a triangle is 110° and one of the non-adjacent interior angles is 60°, the other non-adjacent interior angle is:
questions.explanation: By the exterior angle theorem: exterior angle = sum of two non-adjacent interior angles. So 110° = 60° + other angle → other angle = 50°.
